_source: The pre-intervention evaluation at /morning-report/baseline/. Every word a respondent reads lives in this file — the cohorts, the two scales, the five domains, the measured quantities and the two open questions. The three pages restate none of it, which is what makes the instrument reviewable by somebody who does not read JavaScript.
_why_this_is_separate_from_feedback: feedback.json asks how one session went and is answered after it. This asks what the standing arrangement is like and is answered once, before anything changes. Sharing a file would have meant one of the two instruments bending to fit the other, and a baseline that bends is not a baseline.
_neutrality: This instrument is meant to measure, not to argue. Four things keep it honest, and none of them may be quietly dropped when the wording is next edited:

1. Symmetric anchors. Strongly disagree and Strongly agree sit at equal distance either side of a stated midpoint. Neither end is the expected answer, and no item is introduced by a sentence that implies one.

2. Balanced polarity. The four descriptive domains each carry items worded so that agreeing is favourable and items worded so that agreeing is unfavourable — the ones marked reverse. Somebody who ticks the same column all the way down produces a flat score rather than a good one, and the summary counts those forms instead of hiding them. The overall domain is the deliberate exception: its three items are summary judgements rather than descriptions, and a reversed summary judgement reads as a trick question. The acquiescence check runs across the other four, which is where it has something to compare.
3. A way out that is not the midpoint. No basis to judge is not a 3. It is dropped from the arithmetic entirely, so that people who did not see a thing do not become mild opinion about it.
4. Quantities where a quantity exists. Preparation time is asked for in minutes, not as too much or about right, because the second question cannot be answered without first taking a side.
The open questions are a pair and stay a pair: one asks what should not change, one asks what should. Asking only the second would collect a list of complaints and call it a baseline.
title: Morning report, as it runs today
lede: A picture of the current arrangement, taken before anything about it changes. Five or six minutes, anonymous, and there is no answer here that anybody is hoping for.

wave._note: The wave is what a later round is compared against, so it is part of every record and is set once by whoever hands the link out. Default is the month the form is opened.
wave.label: Round
wave.hint: The measurement round these answers belong to. Leave it as it is unless you were told otherwise.

site.label: Site
site.hint: Where you usually sit for report. Blank is fine.

cohort.title: Which are you?
cohort.lede: The only thing this form asks about you. It is what makes the answers readable — a first-year and a faculty member are describing different experiences of the same twenty-five minutes, and averaging them together would lose both.

context.title: How you take part
context.lede: Neither of these is a judgement about anything. They separate the person who is in the room three times a week from the person who dials in once.

items.label: Sessions you attend in a typical week

agree._note: Five points, a named midpoint, and the two ends the same distance out. The skip is not a point on the scale and is never scored as one.
agree.question: How much do you agree, thinking about the last month or so?

skip.label: No basis to judge
skip.hint: Not a middle answer — this one is left out of the arithmetic.

reverse_note: Reversed item — agreeing with this one counts the other way.

domains.title: Technical
domains.lede: Two sites on one call. This is the half that decides whether the far end could take part at all, and it is asked first because it is the easiest thing to be wrong about from one end of the wire.

items.text: I could hear everyone clearly, wherever I was taking part from.
What was on the shared screen was legible from where I sat.
Getting into the session took me under a minute.
Technical problems interrupted the session.
People on the call could take part as readily as people in the room.
The start was held up by setting the equipment up.

domains.title: Engagement
domains.eyebrow: Who speaks, and what it costs to
domains.lede: Not whether the session was lively. Whether the people in it took part, and what happened to the ones who got something wrong.

items.text: I said something out loud in most sessions I attended.
It was safe to be wrong out loud.
The same few people did most of the talking.
I was asked questions I had a fair chance of answering.
I found my attention going elsewhere.
Senior input left room for someone junior to think out loud first.

domains.title: Learning and education
domains.lede: The educational half: what was taught, at what level, and whether any of it survived the walk back to the wards.

items.text: I left most sessions with something I could use on the wards.
The reasoning was made visible, not just the answer.
The level was pitched about right for the people in the room.
The discussion mostly covered ground I had already covered elsewhere.
I could have said afterwards what the teaching point was.
Comments on how the case was presented were specific enough to act on.

domains.title: Time and burden
domains.eyebrow: What it costs to be there
domains.lede: Time is the one thing here that can be counted rather than rated, so the counting is done a few boxes further down. These four are about the fit between report and the rest of the day.

items.text: The time report takes is time I can afford.
Preparing to present takes more time than I have.
I have arrived late or left early because of clinical duties.
Report ends in time for me to get to where I am due next.

domains.title: Overall experience
domains.lede: The last three, and then one number. Answer these on the arrangement as it stands, not on what it could be.

items.text: I would keep morning report in its current form.
I would describe the current format favourably to someone joining the program.
Report compares well with the other teaching in the program.

measures.title: The countable part
measures.lede: Estimates are fine and nobody checks them. A number that is roughly right is worth more here than a rating that is precisely agreeable — and unlike a rating, a number can be compared to the same number in six months.

items.label: Minutes you spend preparing on a day you are not presenting
items.hint: Reading round the case, looking at the board, anything that counts as getting ready. 0 is an answer.

items.label: Minutes you spend preparing on a day you are presenting
items.hint: The whole preparation, however it is spread. Leave blank if you have never presented.

items.label: Report collides with clinical work I have to deal with there and then
Report runs past its finishing time

global.title: One number
global.eyebrow: The whole thing, on a line
global.question: Overall, morning report as it runs today:
global.lede: Zero and ten are both real answers, and the middle is not the safe one.
global.low: As poor as it could be
global.high: As good as it could be

open.title: In your own words
open.eyebrow: A pair, and it stays a pair
open.lede: Both boxes, or neither, or one — but they are asked together on purpose. A form that only asked the second would come back with a list of complaints and be reported as a baseline.

items.label: What works as it is, and should survive any change
items.placeholder: The parts you would defend if somebody proposed dropping them.

items.label: What you would change, if one thing could change
items.placeholder: One thing, said plainly. Aim it at the arrangement rather than at a person.

storage._note: One lane, not two. Nothing here is written about a named person and nothing joins to the roster, so unlike session feedback there is no half of this that has to be swept. It is a measurement, it is meant to be compared against a later one, and a measurement you delete after seven days cannot be.
storage._naming: Flat files named <wave>--<response id>.json, because the store lists files and not directories.

small_cell._note: A cohort of two is not anonymous in a program this size, whatever the form says at the top. Under this many responses a cohort is reported as a count and nothing else — no mean, no distribution — and its answers are still counted in the all-respondents row.
small_cell.note: Fewer than {n} responses — counted in the total, not broken out. In a group this size a cohort of one or two is not anonymous.

send.relay: Sent to the collection point — it lands in the folder when the facilitator collects it.
send.relay_failed: The collection point could not be reached, so the file was downloaded instead. Hand it over and it can be dropped in by hand.
send.download: No folder and no collection point on this device, so the file was downloaded.

footer: One per person, once. This is the before picture — the point of it is that nothing has changed yet.
thanks: That is the baseline. Thank you.
thanks_note: Nothing you answered is attached to your name, and nothing here is an evaluation of anybody.
